body: @Ikadzuchi77 Do you have a picture of what the screen is suppose to look like? I just get the whole screen as light green in the OpenGL gl_compatbility mode with no hang.

@Sparky015 I forgot to state that the MRP has to be run with Forward+ / Metal, not Compatibility / OpenGL in order for the deadlock to occur. Apologies for leaving that out :( Compatibility does boot to that nice mint-green window like what you ended up with. Launching from a desktop app always deadlocks on the Godot logo screen: Launching within the editor always deadlocks on the grey box: Thanks!

You are good. Sorry, I did actually get the deadlock to occur on 4.7.1 for Metal and Vulkan. I was just checking to make sure that was good to use as a target reference when trying to fix/narrow the issue. I am also getting the hang though for 4.6.3-stable too. I have tried to take a look into it and its appearing like its an issue with the Metal OS driver. Its hanging on the pipeline creation api call on a worker thread, which shouldn't be possible. I ran the project in Instruments and it appears that the compilation does finish, but the pipeline creation call never exits. While investigating, I noticed that if I ran a second instance of godot loading the project on Metal that it would load without a hang which implies some sort of driver cache path (But this does not work when using the Metal validation layer through the MTL_DEBUG_LAYER or MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION environment variables). The Metal validation layer gives no warnings or errors. I tried to extract the problematic shader source and reproduce the hang on the Metal command line compiling tools, but when you attach a binary archive (MTL::BinaryArchive) to pipeline creation, the hang goes away. Additionally, the Metal translation config file that can be extracted from a pipeline via the binary archive was missing, so I couldn't compile the pipeline with metal-tt. All of this combined points more to an issue with the Metal OS driver as I changed nothing about the code except assigning a binary archive instance to the existing archive code (and even without doing that, I could avoid the hang with no code changes when running the two instances of the exact same 4.7.1-stable executable with the same command line args). It could be a combination of invalid pipeline config or invalid shader paired with the driver not handling it well. I am not that confident about this though as the API and shader validation doesn't report anything wrong. I am curious to see what anyone else thinks. I am not sure what to do from here. I tested this with a M1 Pro on macOS 26.6.2.

Tried a few more things based on what you did, no luck on my end either.

Interestingly enough, attaching an empty MTL::BinaryArchive in Godot 4.7.1 (the existing archive field plus setBinaryArchives, and also addRenderPipelineFunctions before PSO create) still deadlocks. The sample just moves to -[AGXG16GFamilyBinaryArchive addRenderPipelineFunctionsWithDescriptor:options:error:], but ends up on the same MTLCompilerConnectionQueue. So no luck on G16/G17.

I dumped the MSL from the hang (CanvasShaderRD family) and compiled it with xcrun -toolchain Metal metal -c. All 82 files compiled, no hang, including the ~180 KB fragment. Offline metal is fine; the live pipeline create is not.

metal-tt can’t finish the job. Default AIR is 2.8 vs target 2.6. With -macos-version-min 26.0 it returns "cannot lower module with unresolved function constants". That matches what you said about the translation config missing from the archive... we never get that script because create-pipeline never returns.

Second Godot instance still hung on both of these machines (tried at 32 s and 70 s).

Apologies... 4.6.3-stable plus this MRP also hangs here, same stack. My earlier "4.6.3 is fine" was based on weaker tests (empty project / load-without-draw), not this zip actually drawing those shaders.

Happy to run anything else on these two systems.

I forgot to mention that I was testing this using Godot from the command line with "--path [path to project] --verbose" as the args. Try with that and see if it changes. I also ran into another weird thing. When I was testing more, somehow the pipeline got cached into the macOS system metal cache, so every time I run the project, I get no more hangs. I tested this on 4.6.3-stable and 4.7.1-stable and both versions got no hang when it was still cached. So I found the system cache and deleted it and the hang returns. However, this did not affect the issue when you run the project through the editor. And with the offline compiling, the shader objects would compile for me too, but I was not able to get the config file to compile the full pipeline even though for me, the pipeline call did finish using the methods I mentioned earlier, so I had access to a the compiled pipeline. I don't know if that is expected or not for the specific pipeline config. You need the config file, either making it by hand or by extracting it from a compiled pipeline to not get the "cannot lower module with unresolved function constants" when compiling the pipeline. I also noticed when testing before that I could comment out all the shaders except one and still get the hang.

	#"res://scripts/display/led_lattice_v4.gdshader",

This is what I see when I pause the debugger at the hang. and this seems to correspond with this in a profiler trace: which is kinda weird as the profiler doesn't show some area as a big hang (even with sampling waiting threads).

It looks like the MTLCompilerService thread doesn't appear when profiling, but that profile triggered a cpu resource report with some stacktraces from the MTLCompilerService. This could be where the hang is coming from as you mentioned that the  com.apple.MTLCompilerConnectionQueue was stuck.

@Sparky015 @migueldeicaza

Apologies for the long silence, was under the weather and haven't touched any code in a long while.


I retested the MRP on both machines this ticket was filed from using:
Godot --path <mrp> --rendering-method forward_plus --rendering-driver metal --verbose

Fresh .godot each run. CLI only, not the editor Play button.

• M4 mini: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Godot 4.7.1.stable.mono.official a13da4feb
• M5 laptop: macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), same Godot build

My conclusion... this actually is not a deadlock. 
While the Godot process sits at ~0% CPU in newRenderPipelineStateWithDescriptor / com.apple.MTLCompilerConnectionQueue (same stack as the original samples), MTLCompilerService is at 100% CPU and growing RSS. It looks hung because the wait is on the compiler XPC, not because the pipeline call never returns.

Compile time from process start until sample no longer showed newRenderPipelineState:

| live `sample_slot()` calls | what I changed | M4 mini | M5 MB |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | one call in `composite_led_rgb` + one in `fragment()` | 15s | 27s |
| 6 | three calls in each of those two sites | 90s | 109s |
| 8 after DCE | Miguel's stub (`halo = vec3(0.0)` instead of `lattice_halo_composite`) | 3m 29s | 3m 35s |
| 16 | original MRP, untouched | 18m 13s | 18m 3s |    

On both machines, Miguel's idea does start. lattice_halo_composite is the only caller of composite_led_rgb, so commenting that call lets those 8 copies DCE and leaves the 8 in fragment(). It just takes a few minutes, which may be why it still looked hung.

During that wait MTLCompilerService sat at 100% CPU and RSS grew past 5 GB on the M4... both systems get nice and toasty!

Same long compile on macOS 27.0.1 as on 26.6.2.

This is Metal compiler cost on a large unrolled sample_slot, not a Godot deadlock. 
An Apple bug report seems like the right next step. 

Happy to run anything else.

@Ikadzuchi77 Good to know it also has the same behavior on the M4 and M5 chips as well. I submitted a bug report to Apple a few days ago, so now I guess we have to wait and see if it can be fixed on their end.
